newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes pressure prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes pressure prices.

text.p: The naphtha market fell with potential arbitrage cargoes putting pressure on levels while gasoline extended Thursday's losses on aggressive offers, traders said on Friday.
At least three offers were seen for both unleaded 95 Ron and 92 Ron gasoline for April loading against no takers.

Offers for a 50,000-barrels cargo of 95-octane gasoline were offered at $27.00-$27.30 per barrel for April 19-23 loading, down from $27.30/$27.50 a day earlier. A trader also offered 92-Ron gasoline at $26.60 per barrel for April 19 to May 4 loading.
Some traders attributed the down trend to the lower levels awarded in the Taiwan reformate tender on Thursday and Wednesday.
"The market is looking to the Taiwan tender for direction and the tender was awarded at fairly lower level," said one trader.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought on Thursday one more unleaded 95-octane reformate at the same $27.40 per barrel it paid for a cargo it bought a day earlier. CPC also bought a leaded 95-octane reformate cargo at $27.70 per barrel cost-and-freight in the tender.
The awards were sharply lower than CPC's previous award for a leaded cargo at $29.00 for April 1-15 delivery and unleaded reformate at a much higher $28.60 April 16-30 arrival.
A major said refinery turnarounds in Asia may help limit the slide in prices in the face of thin demand.
In Singapore, Mobil's 280,000 barrels-per-day refinery was shut since March 15 for a six-week scheduled maintenance turnaround.
Elsewhere in Asia, most South Korean and Japanese refineries turnarounds will also begin in April.
Naphtha prices continue to slide as the market is awash with supplies, traders said.
May swaps fell to be quoted at $21.80/$22.00 per barrel, down from $22.30/$22.50 on Thursday.
Traders said they were looking for price direction from talks for the sale of Saudi Arabian naphtha in the second half of 1997.
Bids were made at below $10.00 per tonne over the Aramco formula, but recent awards from other MidEast suppliers have been made at well above $10.00.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
